ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit in the figure, the left side is a Vsource voltage source, and the upper end is connected through a series resistor labeled Rseries = 470 Ω to the output node on the right; this node is connected downward to ground through a Zener diode labeled Vz = 5.1 V, and at the same time this node is also connected to ground through a load resistor labeled Rload = 6 kΩ. Reasoning: The problem gives Vsource = 5 V. The output node voltage cannot exceed 5 V, while the nominal breakdown voltage of the Zener diode is 5.1 V. Because 5 V is less than 5.1 V, the Zener diode will not enter the reverse breakdown voltage-regulating state, so it is treated as an open circuit. Therefore, the current through the Zener diode is 0 mA.
